PullRequest.Title: Apply agent notebook edits to the open notebook instead of failing
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343214
Refs #344849

## Problem

When an agent host session (Copilot SDK / agent host) asks to change a Jupyter notebook, the Copilot notebook edit tool always fails with `Invalid input, no stream`. The agent then falls back to rewriting the `.ipynb` file on disk. If the notebook is open with unsaved changes (for example after the user typed in a cell, or after running cells, which changes outputs), the editor never shows the agent's change, and saving the notebook removes it again: either through the "content of the file is newer" prompt, where **Overwrite** looks like the right answer because the editor never showed the change, or silently when the file size didn't change. That is the "edits disappear after initially appearing on disk" behavior in #344849.

## Root cause

- The tool only works with a chat response stream. It reads it from `promptContext`, which is only set by [`resolveInput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/editNotebookTool.tsx#L301-L304), and it [throws `Invalid input, no stream`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/editNotebookTool.tsx#L87-L92) without one. Only Copilot Chat's own tool loops call `resolveInput`.
- Agent host sessions run client tools through [`ILanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts#L3444-L3455), which ends in the tool's `invoke` without `resolveInput`, so there is never a stream. `editNotebook` is offered to those sessions through the [Jupyter Notebooks client tool set](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/tools/clientToolSetsContribution.ts#L133-L145), next to `runNotebookCell` and `getNotebookSummary`, which don't need a stream. So the agent can run cells (making the notebook dirty) and read the in-memory notebook, but can't edit it.
- When the agent writes the file instead, a dirty notebook is [never reloaded](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/storedFileWorkingCopyManager.ts#L276-L279), and the save conflict only offers [Overwrite or Revert](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/services/workingCopy/common/storedFileWorkingCopy.ts#L1151-L1156) (no Compare, unlike text files). The agent host review that reconciles text files after agent writes [skips notebooks](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostEditReview.ts#L527-L530).

## Fix

In `editNotebookTool.tsx`, when there is no chat response stream, the tool now collects the same notebook edits (insert or delete cells) and cell text edits it would have sent to the stream into a `WorkspaceEdit` and applies it with `IWorkspaceService.applyEdit`. The edit lands in the open notebook model, next to any unsaved changes, so the editor shows it right away and a normal save keeps it. If the edit can't be applied, the tool fails with a clear error instead of reporting success. The result also tells the model that the edit is in the open notebook and may not be saved yet, so it shouldn't rewrite the `.ipynb` on disk.

Local Copilot Chat is unchanged: when `resolveInput` provided a stream for this request, the edits still go through it (chat editing session, Keep/Undo). The no-stream path follows the same pattern as the built-in rename tool, which applies its edits with the bulk edit service when there is no chat context.

The tool also no longer reuses a prompt context from another request. There is a single `EditNotebookTool` instance ([created once](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/vscode-node/toolsService.ts#L97) and [registered once](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/vscode-node/tools.ts#L32-L35)), and `resolveInput` stores the prompt context, including its stream, on it until the next local tool call. Without a check, an agent session call after an earlier Copilot Chat request would use that request's finished stream and fail with `Response stream has been closed` (the new unit tests reproduce this on `main`). The tool now uses the stored context only when its `requestId` matches the invocation's `chatRequestId`. The Copilot Chat tool loop passes the same value to both: it calls [`resolveInput` with the prompt context](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx#L297) whose [`requestId`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx#L181) it also passes as [`chatRequestId`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/panel/toolCalling.tsx#L322) (the turn id, [always set](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/toolCallingLoop.ts#L454)), and VS Code carries `chatRequestId` [to the main thread](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts#L130) and [back to the tool](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModelTools.ts#L194). Agent sessions don't set `chatRequestId`, and other chat requests have their own, so they get the workspace edit path. Inline chat never offers this tool, so requiring a request id doesn't change it.

Not changed, possible follow-ups:
- Edits applied this way are not part of the agent session's edit review or checkpoints and are left unsaved, like the rename tool's fallback.
- Dirty notebooks still don't reload or merge external changes, and the notebook save conflict still has no Compare action. The file service's same-size check is unchanged.

## Before / after

Both recordings use a small test extension that calls the notebook edit tool the way agent sessions do (`vscode.lm.invokeTool('copilot_editNotebook', …)` with no chat stream) and, like the agent, writes the cell into the `.ipynb` on disk if the tool fails. The notebook has an unsaved edit (` # checked`) when the agent adds its cell.

### Before

![Before: the notebook edit tool fails with "Invalid input, no stream", the cell is written to disk but never shows in the editor, saving reports that the file is newer, and after Overwrite the agent's cell is gone](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/3fb31f240f522943649d00894da2ae6f971a070d/20261015-171820-C17-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

![After: the agent's cell appears in the open notebook right away, the save completes without a conflict, and both the agent's cell and the user's edit are kept](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/3fb31f240f522943649d00894da2ae6f971a070d/20261015-171820-C17-F1/after.gif?raw=true)

## How to test

1. In a dev build of this branch, signed in to Copilot (or with a BYOK model, so Copilot's tools are registered), open a folder with a Python `.ipynb` and open it in the notebook editor.
2. Type in a cell so the notebook has unsaved changes.
3. From an agent host session, ask the agent to add a cell to the notebook. Or call the tool directly from an extension: `vscode.lm.invokeTool('copilot_editNotebook', { input: { filePath, editType: 'insert', cellId: 'BOTTOM', newCode: 'print(1)', language: 'python' }, toolInvocationToken: undefined })`.
4. The new cell appears in the open notebook. Save: there's no conflict, and the file on disk has the new cell and your edit.
5. On `main`, step 3 fails with `Invalid input, no stream`.

<details><summary>Automated repro: test extension, workspace and scenario</summary>

Create the workspace with `node reset-ws.cjs <tmp>/nb-edit-proof/ws`, launch Code OSS signed in on that folder with `--extensionDevelopmentPath=<probe-ext folder>`, then run `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>`. It fails on `main` and passes with this PR.

`probe-ext/extension.js`

```js
// Calls the Copilot notebook edit tool the way agent sessions do: through the tools service,
// without a chat response stream. When the tool fails, it falls back to writing the cell into the
// .ipynb on disk, which is what the agent does in that case.
const vscode = require('vscode');
const fs = require('fs');

const TOOL = 'copilot_editNotebook';
const CODE = 'print("cell added by the agent")';

exports.activate = context => {
	context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand('notebookEditToolProbe.addCell', async () => {
		const notebook = vscode.window.activeNotebookEditor?.notebook;
		if (!notebook) {
			vscode.window.showErrorMessage('Open a notebook first.');
			return;
		}
		try {
			await vscode.lm.invokeTool(TOOL, {
				input: { filePath: notebook.uri.fsPath, editType: 'insert', cellId: 'BOTTOM', newCode: CODE, language: 'python', explanation: 'Add a cell at the end' },
				toolInvocationToken: undefined,
			});
			vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Agent: the notebook edit tool added the cell.');
		} catch (error) {
			const json = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebook.uri.fsPath, 'utf8'));
			json.cells.push({ cell_type: 'code', execution_count: null, metadata: {}, outputs: [], source: [CODE] });
			fs.writeFileSync(notebook.uri.fsPath, JSON.stringify(json, null, 1) + '\n');
			vscode.window.showErrorMessage(`Agent: the notebook edit tool failed (${error.message}), so the agent wrote the cell to the file on disk.`);
		}
	}));
};
```

```js
// Writes a fresh two-cell Python notebook into the workspace folder given as the first argument.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const dir = process.argv[2];
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });

		{ cell_type: 'markdown', metadata: {}, source: ['# Sales report'] },
```

`repro.cjs`

```js
// Agent edits to an open, unsaved notebook land in the editor and survive saving.
//
// Run against a Code OSS window that is signed in to Copilot, opened on the workspace written by
// reset-ws.cjs (os.tmpdir()/nb-edit-proof/ws), with the probe extension in ./probe-ext loaded via
// --extensionDevelopmentPath. The probe's command calls the Copilot notebook edit tool through
// vscode.lm.invokeTool without a chat response stream, which is how agent sessions call it, and, like
// the agent, writes the cell to the .ipynb on disk if the tool fails.
const fs = require('fs');
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');

const NOTEBOOK_FILE = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'nb-edit-proof', 'ws', 'report.ipynb');
const AGENT_CODE = 'print("cell added by the agent")';
const USER_TEXT = '# checked';

const normalize = text => (text || '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ');

async function notebookCells(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => {
		return [...document.querySelectorAll('.notebookOverlay .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row')]
			.map(row => [...row.querySelectorAll('.view-line')].map(line => line.textContent).join('\n'));
	}).then(cells => cells.map(normalize));
}

async function activeTabIsDirty(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty'));
}

async function waitFor(ctx, predicate, timeoutMs, what) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	for (; ;) {
		const value = await predicate();
		if (value) {
			return value;
		}
		if (Date.now() > end) {
			throw new Error(`Timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
		}
		await ctx.sleep(200);
	}
}

module.exports = {
	id: 'agent-notebook-edit-open-dirty',
	title: 'Agent edits to an open, unsaved notebook land in the editor and survive saving',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344849',
	stepPauseMs: 1200,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'S1',
			title: 'The notebook is open with two cells',
			async run(ctx) {
				await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-workbench .part.editor')), 30000, 'the workbench');
				if (!(await ctx.page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.notebookOverlay .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row')))) {
					await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+P');
					await ctx.page.locator('.quick-input-widget input').waitFor();
					await ctx.page.keyboard.type('report.ipynb', { delay: 30 });
					await ctx.page.locator('.quick-input-widget .monaco-list-row', { hasText: 'report.ipynb' }).first().waitFor();
					await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				}
				const cells = await waitFor(ctx, async () => {
					const c = await notebookCells(ctx.page);
					return c.length === 2 && c.some(text => text.includes('total = 40 + 2')) ? c : undefined;
				}, 30000, 'the notebook editor to show both cells');
				if (!fs.readFileSync(NOTEBOOK_FILE, 'utf8').includes('total = 40 + 2')) {
					throw new Error('The notebook file on disk is not the expected fixture');
				}
				return `Notebook editor shows ${cells.length} cells`;
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S2',
			title: 'The user edits the code cell without saving',
			async run(ctx) {
				const line = ctx.page.locator('.notebookOverlay .monaco-list-row .view-line', { hasText: 'print(total)' }).first();
				await line.click();
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('End');
				await ctx.page.keyboard.type(`  ${USER_TEXT}`, { delay: 40 });
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Escape');
				await waitFor(ctx, () => activeTabIsDirty(ctx.page), 5000, 'the notebook to become dirty');
				return 'The notebook has unsaved changes';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S3',
			title: 'The agent adds a cell with the notebook edit tool',
			async run(ctx) {
				await ctx.runCommand('Agent: Add a Cell to the Open Notebook');
				const toast = await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => {
					const messages = [...document.querySelectorAll('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast .notification-list-item-message')];
					return messages.map(t => t.textContent || '').find(t => t.includes('Agent:'));
				}), 30000, 'the agent to report back');
				await ctx.sleep(1500);
				return `Agent reported: ${toast.trim().slice(0, 160)}`;
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S4',
			title: 'The user saves the notebook',
			async run(ctx) {
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+S');
				const outcome = await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => {
					const conflict = [...document.querySelectorAll('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast')]
						.find(t => (t.textContent || '').includes('content of the file is newer'));
					if (conflict) {
						return 'conflict';
					}
					return document.querySelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty') ? undefined : 'saved';
				}), 10000, 'the save to finish');
				if (outcome === 'conflict') {
					// The editor never showed the agent's cell, so overwriting looks like the right choice.
					await ctx.sleep(1500);
					await ctx.page.locator('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast', { hasText: 'content of the file is newer' })
						.locator('.monaco-button', { hasText: 'Overwrite' }).first().click();
					await waitFor(ctx, async () => !(await activeTabIsDirty(ctx.page)), 10000, 'the overwrite to finish');
					return 'Save reported that the file on disk is newer; the user chose Overwrite';
				}
				return 'Saved without a conflict';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S5',
			title: "The agent's cell is in the editor and in the saved file",
			async run(ctx) {
				await ctx.sleep(1000);
				const cells = await notebookCells(ctx.page);
				const disk = fs.readFileSync(NOTEBOOK_FILE, 'utf8');
				const inEditor = cells.some(text => text.includes(AGENT_CODE));
				const onDisk = disk.includes(AGENT_CODE.replace(/"/g, '\\"'));
				const userEditKept = disk.includes(USER_TEXT);
				if (!inEditor || !onDisk || !userEditKept) {
					throw new Error(`Agent cell in editor: ${inEditor}, agent cell on disk: ${onDisk}, user edit on disk: ${userEditKept} (editor shows ${cells.length} cells)`);
				}
				return `Editor shows ${cells.length} cells including the agent's; the saved file has the agent's cell and the user's edit`;
			},
		},
	],
};
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Chat edits one notebook cell with a matching request id and response stream
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the notebook URI, open or reuse the notebook document, compute one insert/delete/text edit, emit it to the existing chat response stream, wait for document-change events, then render the bounded tool result. The diff's request-id comparison and stream selection are constant-time; `workspace.applyEdit` is not reached.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and deserialize the notebook if it is not already open; otherwise reuse the in-memory document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open per tool invocation; warm open notebooks use `findNotebook` and perform no filesystem load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same open/reuse call ran after the old stream validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold notebook loading blocks edit preparation; warm reuse does not cross the filesystem boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one logical notebook cell operation or one cell text replacement through the chat response stream, bracketed by existing start/end notebook-edit notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical edit per invocation; no loop creates per-cell boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Matching chat invocations used the same response-stream calls before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The authoritative edit and resulting change events must complete before the result is rendered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Notebook cell count controls pre-existing in-memory scans; replacement text size controls the one edit payload. Effective boundary cardinality remains one logical edit per invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The tool issues one edit for this invocation and awaits existing event completion. No changed loop, `Promise.all`, limiter, or concurrency burst is present.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An already-open notebook is the warm state and avoids loading; a cold document is opened once. No new cache, cache key, miss retry, or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: request-id matching selects the unchanged stream path, and the new `instanceof WorkspaceEditStream` branch is therefore skipped.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notebook sizes and stream implementation latency vary, but those costs and their scaling are unchanged on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the normal chat path retains its prior expensive boundaries and multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host or tools-service invocation edits one cell without a chat response stream
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve and open/reuse the notebook, construct a single `WorkspaceEdit`, call `workspace.applyEdit` once, wait for the corresponding document events, and render the result. The newly enabled apply is on the critical path because the tool must update the open notebook before returning.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and deserialize the notebook when it is not already in `workspace.notebookDocuments`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold open per invocation; normally zero loads for the target open notebook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old no-stream validation failed before attempting to open the notebook.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold open blocks edit construction; warm open notebooks avoid the load.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply the collected notebook edit or cell text edit through VS Code's `workspace.applyEdit`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one `applyEdit` call containing one logical cell operation per successful tool invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Streamless invocations failed immediately and applied no edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call is awaited and its document-change events are required before the tool result can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Render the existing notebook edit result after the edit completes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per successful invocation; insertion summaries inspect the notebook once, while edit/delete return a fixed message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Streamless invocations failed before result rendering; successful chat invocations already used this renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Result rendering occurs after the authoritative apply and is part of response completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One operation is accepted by the tool schema. Existing notebook scans scale linearly with cell count, and a text replacement payload scales with the target cell's new text; there is no per-cell I/O or IPC fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One apply is awaited per invocation. The change does not spawn parallel applies or add a collection-wide `Promise.all`; separate external invocations are not coalesced, but the diff provides no realistic burst mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The open-document collection is the warm state; no additional cache is created. Cold opening happens once, and failures are not retried by the changed code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch, tool schema, and workspace service implementation directly establish a single awaited apply boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large notebooks can make the pre-existing scans and rendering more expensive, but the newly added boundary remains one operation and is necessary to provide the newly supported streamless edit behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the PR intentionally turns a previously rejected invocation into one bounded notebook edit, without fan-out, repeated boundary work, or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invocation ignores a stale response stream from an earlier chat request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The request-id check rejects the stale context, then follows the same single-`WorkspaceEdit` path as a streamless agent invocation; the stale stream receives no calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply one collected cell operation via `workspace.applyEdit` rather than attempting the stale chat stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One apply per invocation, independent of notebook cell count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old code reused whatever stream was stored in `promptContext`; it did not call `workspace.applyEdit`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The one apply and resulting events gate completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One tool operation and one edit payload; notebook size affects only existing in-memory preparation/result work.
